observation_summary: Deserialization of a nested reference type (e.g., AtomicReference<AtomicReference<T>>) with a null value results in an incorrect object structure instead of the expected null-wrapped value.
reasoning_summary: The defect arises because the deserializer and the null value provider for a bean property were not kept in sync during contextual deserialization. When a new contextual deserializer was created, the property's null value provider remained stale, causing it to return a default object (e.g., an empty AtomicReference) instead of the correctly nested null value expected by the type hierarchy. The fix ensures that if the deserializer and null provider were originally linked, the null provider is updated to match the new deserializer.
